'''''Chamaemelum fuscatum''''', commonly known as '''dusky dogfennel''' or '''dark chamomile''', is an annual herb in the family Asteraceae, native to Europe and introduced to California.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Chamaemelum fuscatum'' (Brot.) Vasc. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:192458-1 |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> 

''C. fuscatum''  typically grows from 5 to 20 cm tall, but some specimens have reached over 35 cm. Leaves are [[pinnately divided]] and between 1 and 4 centimetres long. They are rounded into ellipses, with those closer to the stem sized smaller and more [[Ovate (botany)|ovate]]. Like other members of the ''[[Asteraceae]]'' family, the flowers are actually [[Astercacea#Floral heads|composite flowers]]. The outer ray flowers are the largest at 8 to 15 mm long, while the inner disk flowers measure between 2.5 and 3 mm long. Both flowers produce similar-sized fruits<ref name=berkeley>{{Cite web |title=''Chamaemelum fuscatum'' |url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=2010 |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=ucjeps.berkeley.edu}}</ref> and, in California, bloom between March and April.<ref name="berkeley" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=C''hamaemelum fuscatum'' Calflora |url=https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=1917 |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=www.calflora.org}}</ref>
